question: Will the 2-year Treasury yield dip below 4.55% in October?

frozen_rule.source: Department of the Treasury, Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates, year 2026, table column '2 Yr'.
frozen_rule.metric_and_unit: U.S. Treasury 2-year par yield / constant maturity Treasury (CMT) rate, percent per annum.
frozen_rule.geography: United States Treasury securities; this is the U.S. Treasury daily par-yield curve, not a local or foreign yield series.
frozen_rule.comparison: Strictly lower than 4.55% (below, not equal to).
frozen_rule.qualifying_observation_dates: Any listed daily source date from October 2 through October 31, 2026, inclusive.
frozen_rule.resolution_timing: Frozen rule says resolve as soon as a qualifying daily value is published, or once data is available for the last business day of October. If no qualifying value is published and last-business-day data is not available by November 13, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, resolve No.
frozen_rule.intraday_vs_daily: Contract source is a daily table with one 2 Yr value per date; it does not define an intraday crossing test. Treasury describes CMT values as read from its daily par curve at fixed maturities and says the input quotes are indicative bid-side quotations obtained by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York at or near 3:30 PM each trading day. This does not establish continuous intraday observation or a timezone for that quote time.
frozen_rule.calendar_and_timezone: Source observations are labeled by calendar date and exist on business days. The frozen market's deadline is explicitly Eastern Time. The captured Treasury description says 'at or near 3:30 PM each trading day' but does not state a timezone in the relevant passage; do not conflate the deadline timezone with quote time.
frozen_rule.market_description_verbatim: This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 2-year yield is lower than the listed value for any date between October 2, 2026 and October 31, 2026. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

observations.table_window_checked: 2026-10-02 through 2026-10-19, inclusive; dates in the frozen rule's window for which Treasury had published rows at retrieval time.
observations.unit: percent per annum; Treasury table values displayed to two decimal places.
observations.cross_check: The HTML table and its linked CSV export agree on every displayed in-window business-day 2 Yr observation. The CSV contains 200 data rows through October 19, 2026.
observations.limited_factual_result: No published in-window daily 2 Yr value through October 19 is below 4.55%; the lowest displayed value in the checked window is 4.74% on October 16. This is a current-source observation only and says nothing about later October dates.

separate_proxy_note: This is the exact named Treasury resolution source, not a FRED daily-series proxy or an intraday Treasury-market quote. No proxy data was used.
unknowns: Treasury had not published later October daily rows at retrieval time; October 20 and subsequent dates remain unobserved in this capture.
The page/CSV does not state a precise publication timestamp for each daily row; response Date and retrieval timestamps record capture time, not source publication time.
The frozen rule provides a November 13 ET fallback deadline if qualifying data and last-business-day data are not published, but the final resolution event remains in the future.
A FRED series or secondary market price would not be the named contract source and was not substituted.
